Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-04 16:30 PST
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Carlos Ramirez (Skybridge CTO), Maya Lin (Skybridge Head of Platform), Evan Wu (Skybridge SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Redwood demo focused on rate limiting, quotas, and multi-tenant keys (org/project). Customer concerned about per-tenant limits, burst behavior, and mapping to their API keys. Discussed hosted vs dedicated and VPC implications. Action items: send pricing, share org/project keys doc, schedule security follow-up.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining 

 uh we got about 45 minutes on the calendar, I'm Jordan with Redwood, this is Priya, our systems engineer. How's everybody doing?
[00:07] Carlos: Good, thanks. Sorry got pulled into two things but we're here.
[00:10] Maya: Morning from my side, excited to see the rate limit stuff.
[00:14] Priya: Cool, quick agenda: we'll walk the console demo for org and project keys, show per-route quotas and token limits, then Q&A and next steps.
[00:21] Evan: Sounds good, our main ask is how to enforce tenant isolation and avoid noisy neighbor impact — we need soft and hard quotas.
[00:27] Jordan: Perfect, that's exactly what we'll demo. Quick qual question — are you running a single multi-tenant service or separate stacks per customer?
[00:33] Carlos: Multi-tenant single stack right now, we shard at the app layer. We want to use Redwood to centralize inference and have per-tenant caps. Also we need audit logs for compliance.
[00:41] Priya: Great, that's typical. We'll show org-level defaults and per-project overrides — think org = Skybridge, project = customer account or internal env.
[00:49] [00:46] Jordan: Priya, do you want to share screen?
[00:48] Priya: Yep sharing now. Can you see the Redwood Console?
[00:51] Maya: Yep we can.
[00:53] Priya: Okay top left you'll see Org settings — here we set global token budget, default per-project RPS, and burst window. So org defaults provide a safety net.
[01:05] [01:03] Carlos: When you say token budget, is that per minute, hour?
[01:06] Priya: We support multiple quota units — tokens per minute, tokens per day, and request counts per second. You can mix them. For example you might do 100,000 tokens/day org-wide and 200 rps peak per project.
[01:16] Evan: How does bursting work? If one tenant suddenly spikes, will it steal capacity from others?
[01:20] Priya: We have configurable burst capacity and isolate using project keys; by default the runtime enforces per-project hard limits and a shared pool for excess if you enable burst. You can also disable burst so hard limits block.
[01:30] [01:28] Jordan: To add, on Dedicated you get reserved GPU capacity and you can map partitions to project groups so noisy neighbor is minimized.
[01:36] Carlos: Are the mappings automatic? We need to understand operational overhead.
[01:39] Priya: You can do automatic placement or pin projects to specific GPU pools. The console shows a mapping view and you can create autoscale rules per pool.
[01:45] [01:44] Maya: Show us an example rule please.
[01:46] Priya: Sure — creating an autoscale policy: min 2 workers, max 20, scale on token/sec threshold. You can tie that to a schedule as well.
[01:55] [01:53] Evan: For our compliance team, encryption at rest and KMS integration is a requirement. Where does that show?
[01:57] Priya: Under Security -> Keys. For Private deployments or Dedicated we integrate with your KMS/HSM; for hosted we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS. We also stream audit logs into your S3 or SIEM.
[02:08] Carlos: And SSO? We use Okta.
[02:10] Jordan: SAML/SSO is supported, RBAC roles in the console, and you can restrict who can change quotas.
[02:16] [02:15] Maya: On the API side, how do we pass the project key? Is it header-based?
[02:18] Priya: We have org/project API keys. You set X-Redwood-Project: <project-key> header. We also support API keys per route if you want more granularity.
[02:27] Jordan: Note: keys can be scoped to only embeddings or only generation endpoints so you can limit surface area.
[02:33] [02:32] Evan: If a key leaks, can we rotate it without downtime?
[02:35] Priya: Yep, keys support versioning and immediate revoke. We also have ephemeral short-lived keys if you want.
[02:40] [02:38] Carlos: Let's dive into an example — we have three customer tiers: free / pro / enterprise. We want free to have 10k tokens/day, pro 200k/day, enterprise unlimited but with per-second guardrails.
[02:51] Priya: You can set per-project quotas for each customer project; we recommend org defaults for safety then override at project level for tiers. For enterprise you can set a soft daily quota + a higher hard rps limit.
[03:01] [02:59] Jordan: I'll show the API demo quickly — hitting the generation endpoint with a project key and showing quota headers. Priya, can you open the API console?
[03:07] Priya: Yep — in the request you'll see response headers: x-redwood-remaining-tokens, x-redwood-quota-reset, x-redwood-rate-limit. Those are helpful for app-level throttling.
[03:17] Evan: Those headers are critical, we'll use them to backpressure our workers.
[03:20] Maya: How accurate are remaining token counters when streaming responses?
[03:24] Priya: The counters are approximate during streaming but converge at completion. We also offer a preflight token estimate endpoint if you want exact consumption before sending long prompts.
[03:34] [03:32] Carlos: Any SLA differences between hosted and dedicated around throttling?
[03:36] Jordan: Hosted has tenant-level soft limits and we have clear throttling behaviors; Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and SLA-backed throughput so throttling is less likely — but you still configure quotas per project.
[03:46] [03:44] Evan: Want to talk about metrics — where do we see usage and chargeback per tenant?
[03:48] Priya: In the Console billing -> Usage you can break down token consumption by project, route, model, and time windows. We also export CSVs and have a billing API.
[03:58] Jordan: We built Redwood Optimize to give batching suggestions — e.g., if a tenant has many small requests we suggest batching to reduce unit cost and decrease RPS.
[04:06] Maya: Can optimize changes be applied automatically or are they suggestions?
[04:09] Priya: Suggestions by default; advanced plans can enable auto-apply for batching or caching rules, but we usually recommend manual review first.
[04:16] [04:14] Carlos: Any mention about privacy / data residency? Some of our customers require EU-only hosting.
[04:18] Jordan: We support region-specific deployments and can pin projects to EU clusters; audit logs and data residency options are in the Private offering.
[04:26] Evan: On failures, what's behavior — queued requests, immediate 429s?
[04:28] Priya: Configurable. You can set queue depth and backpressure thresholds; by default we return 429 when quotas are exhausted. With Dedicated you can enable a short burst queue.
[04:36] [04:35] Carlos: Can we set different behaviors per project? For example, enterprise gets queued but free gets immediate 429.
[04:39] Priya: Yes, per-project error handling policies are supported.
[04:42] [04:40] Jordan: I'm going to show the policy editor — create a policy named "free-tier-throttle": hard limit 10k/day, immediate 429, route restrict generation endpoint only. You can attach that to a group of projects.
[04:52] [04:50] Maya: Nice, can you show the audit log entry for when a limit is hit?
[04:53] Priya: Click on Audit -> Events -> filter quota_exceeded. Here's an entry: timestamp, project_id, rule_id, consumed_tokens. You can export or push to your SIEM.
[05:03] Evan: Good, that maps to our SOC2 control.
[05:05] Carlos: A couple of nitty-gritty things — do you support org-wide rate limits that are token-based but also have per-route overrides?
[05:10] Priya: Yes, rule precedence: project override wins, then org defaults, then model-level fallbacks. You can also create per-route rules that only apply to a model family.
[05:20] Jordan: Quick pause — any red flags so far?
[05:22] Carlos: Nothing major; we want to validate the exact behavior under load. We'll want you to run a controlled benchmark with our traffic patterns.
[05:27] Jordan: Totally, we can do a pilot and run a POC with representative traces. We'll show expert-mode logs and kernel-level metrics for Dedicated so you can see tail-latency.
[05:36] [05:34] Maya: On the POC: what do you need from us?
[05:36] Priya: A sample workload, list of 3 critical customer projects, and success criteria (latency p95, cost per 1M tokens, and quota enforcement behavior).
[05:45] Carlos: We'll put that together. Also security docs please — SOC2, ISO, network diagram.
[05:50] Jordan: I'll include our security pack and a dedicated vs hosted comparison doc.
[05:53] [05:52] Evan: One last question on keys rotation — do you have a key per project or per environment?
[05:57] Priya: We recommend per-project keys for tenant isolation. You can also generate short-lived ephemeral keys from a project key for temporary consumers.
[06:07] [06:05] Jordan: Alright let's recap next steps. I'll send pricing and Dedicated options; Priya will share org/project keys guide and example configuration; Carlos will schedule a security review. Any other asks?
[06:16] Carlos: Can you include a sample nginx ingress config for passing headers?
[06:19] Priya: Yep will include a snippet.
[06:21] Maya: And the quota headers example in JSON response shape please.
[06:24] Jordan: Great. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email and Slack.
[06:28] [END OF TRANSCRIPT]

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-heard product names (e.g., "Redwood Dedicate" instead of Dedicated), filler words left in. References to shared artifacts: pricing deck (link in follow-up), security pack (link in follow-up), POC questionnaire (shared with AE).
